metrics.name: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index
metrics.what: An average of ten hard tests (coding, agents, science, reasoning) run the same way for every model. The best single 'how smart is it' number.

metrics.name: SWE-bench Pro
metrics.what: Fix real bugs in real open-source projects; the fix only counts if the project's own tests pass. Scores are reported by each maker with their own setup.

metrics.name: Terminal-Bench 2
metrics.what: Finish multi-step jobs in a Linux terminal: set up servers, debug builds, crunch data. All scores from one independent run by Vals AI with the same setup for every model, because makers' own numbers differ by up to 30 points.

metrics.name: BrowseComp
metrics.what: Track down hard-to-find facts by browsing the web over many steps.

metrics.name: GPQA Diamond
metrics.what: PhD-level biology, chemistry and physics questions you can't just Google. Top models are now near the ceiling, so small gaps mean little.

metrics.name: Humanity's Last Exam (no tools)
metrics.what: Expert questions from 100+ fields, written specifically to stump AI. Answered without tools. Independent Artificial Analysis runs where they exist, otherwise the maker's own number (marked).

metrics.name: ARC-AGI-2
metrics.what: Visual puzzles the model has never seen. Measures learning on the spot, not memory. Scores verified by the ARC Prize foundation.

metrics.name: MMMU-Pro
metrics.what: College-level questions that require reading images, diagrams and charts. Independent Artificial Analysis runs only.

metrics.name: Arena text leaderboard (Elo)
metrics.what: Blind votes from real users on which answer was better. A higher Elo means people preferred it more often. New models with few votes can still move a lot.
